newsitem.title: USA: Seagram's Universal Studios ends pact with Bubble Factory.
newsitem.headline: Seagram's Universal Studios ends pact with Bubble Factory.

text.p: Universal Studios and The Bubble Factory, a two-year-old production company led by former MCA President Sid Sheinberg, ended an exclusive production agreement.
Termination of the pact, formed in July 1995, comes on the heels of several box office flops resulting from the collaboration, such as "McHale's Navy" and "Flipper," industry sources said.

The Bubble Factory was set up by Sheinberg and his two sons, Jon and Bill, after he left his position at MCA, the parent of Universal. The entire entity, which changed its name to Universal last December, is a unit of Seagram Co. Ltd.
Under the agreement, which was open-ended, Universal was to finance three to four Bubble Factory films per year, a source familiar with the situation said.

"We have great respect for Sid Sheinberg and all that he has accomplished. The previous arrangement with The Bubble Factory was mutually too restrictive and limiting to both parties," Universal Studios President Ron Meyer said in a statement.

"We believe that entering into this new arrangement at this time will serve the best interests of both parties, eliminate unproductive stresses, and hopefully result in future successful films," said Sheinberg.

In addition to the motion picture arrangement, a joint venture agreement between MCA Records, a label in the Universal Music group, and The Track Factory, an affiliate of The Bubble Factory, is being terminated.
Formed primarily as a vehicle for Bubble Factory soundtrack exploitation, the Track Factory joint venture has just released Sammy Hagar's new album "Marching to Mars." Sammy Hagar
will continue as an artist on MCA Records, Universal said.
